gateProvenAbleToFire.rule: DEV_PROCESS 2.2 and 2.3 — a gating indicator is tested for its ability to fire, on the real exit code
gateProvenAbleToFire.syntheticProofs: 13 negative fixtures inside the test file, one per violation class, each asserting the returned selector and value rather than a boolean. Plus a positive control asserting a conformant fixture returns zero, so a checker that always fired would fail too.
gateProvenAbleToFire.realFileProof: Two regressions were injected into web/shell.css itself (.navgroup > .gl back to 10px, .panel-head .t back to 620 13px/18px). `npm test` reported 114 pass / 3 fail and exited 1, naming: 'shell.css:468  .navgroup > .gl  [floor]  10px' and 'shell.css:159  .panel-head .t  [ramp]  620 13px/18px — is not the head step, which is 620 15px/22px'. The file was then restored and the suite returned to 117/0.
gateProvenAbleToFire.exitCodeChecked: 1 on the negative run, 0 on the restored run, read from the node --test process, not from a pipe

adversarialFindingsThisPhase.finding: My own verification check reported the metrics two-column rule present when it was not.
adversarialFindingsThisPhase.cause: The grep string `repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr))` also matches the pre-existing rule inside the 900px media query, so it could never return false. A check that cannot fail is not a check — the same defect class the guard test was written to avoid, committed by me while writing it.
adversarialFindingsThisPhase.consequence: The rule had in fact been reverted by a before/after CSS swap used to capture comparison screenshots, and the false-positive check hid it. Caught by reading `git diff`, which showed the 1180 block unchanged.
adversarialFindingsThisPhase.fix: Re-applied and re-verified by extracting the 1180 media block specifically and asserting the rule is inside THAT block, then confirming the file-wide count is 2 (900 block plus 1180 block).

adversarialFindingsThisPhase.finding: The measurement harness reported a 500px floor on window widths of 390 and 480.
adversarialFindingsThisPhase.cause: Its own output <pre> sat in normal flow and forced a minimum body width, and separately headless Chrome on this machine clamps window.innerWidth at about 500 CSS px.
adversarialFindingsThisPhase.consequence: The narrow-width top-bar comparison was contaminated and could not have supported the conclusion I was about to draw from it.
adversarialFindingsThisPhase.fix: Took the output block out of flow, re-measured, and restricted the reported conclusion to widths the instrument can actually reach: 620px and above. Below roughly 545px the top bar now overflows where it previously fit, which is reported as a finding rather than presented as verified at 390px.

adversarialFindingsThisPhase.finding: The four metric keys were already being destroyed on main at 960px.
adversarialFindingsThisPhase.evidence: P:/tmp/g76-shots/before-960-metrics.png, captured from origin/main's shell.css, shows NEED..., OVER..., PERM..., MEET... — the label is gone, not shortened.
adversarialFindingsThisPhase.consequence: Raising the key to the 12px floor would have made a pre-existing information-loss defect worse.
adversarialFindingsThisPhase.fix: Dropped white-space: nowrap and the ellipsis so the key wraps, and dropped the metric strip to two columns at the existing 1180px breakpoint. Every key now reads in full at 960px.

adversarialFindingsThisPhase.finding: Two heredoc-written scripts silently had their backslash escapes collapsed into real newlines, producing a broken multi-line string in one case and a JavaScript syntax error in the other.
adversarialFindingsThisPhase.consequence: The first failed loudly because every replacement asserts exactly one match. The second failed SILENTLY: the harness rendered, reported nothing, and would have been read as 'no measurements available'.
adversarialFindingsThisPhase.fix: Replaced every escape with String.fromCharCode, and the test file itself now carries a CRLF fixture so the same class of bug cannot reach the guard.

adversarialFindingsThisPhase.finding: A port probe returned HTTP 200 on 8098 from another lane's Plan Review server.
adversarialFindingsThisPhase.consequence: One screenshot captured another lane's application. No write, no kill, no interference — but it proves a 200 is not proof of whose server answered.
adversarialFindingsThisPhase.fix: Moved to a verified-free port and confirmed the served content contained the expected markup before trusting any capture.
